hypothesis: One native reward-conditioned cue association can be combined with multiple independently addressable episode slots; concurrent task retention should beat a one-slot R4 baseline, but not a matched conventional Python dict.
architecture: Original untouched R4 CueCells is retained for shared reward-conditioned match/different synaptic counts; R5 adds authenticated task-identity keyed episodic cue values. Max eight active slots. No hidden MemoryEnv goal coordinates, semantic oracle or extra training labels.
learning: Same real physically observed early cue per slot, same original terminal reward updates as R4 FIT. No new parameters fitted on CHECK or DEV. Slot binding is explicit architecture, not an autonomously discovered representation.
controls: Strong equal-information conventional slot-to-cue dictionary with same R4-equivalent learned reward success/failure table; original R4 single cue; R5 one-slot ablation; semantic equality upper bound.
stopping: Fail closed on capacity overflow, duplicate slots, unsupported tokens and invalid reward; source only qualification before physical first use.
limits: This does not demonstrate native superiority over a conventional associative memory, autonomous goal-directed behavior, interference from learned semantic competition or compositional cognitive generalization.
